title: Server sim clock is setInterval(16.67 ms) with no accumulator: runs at ~33 Hz on Windows dev, ~4% fast on Linux, and drifts from wall time
description: stepRoom advances exactly one FIXED_STEP per timer callback and never measures wall time. Node timers have integer-ms resolution and Windows timer granularity is ~15.6 ms, so on the user's Windows machine (where npm run dev:all playtests happen) the authoritative sim runs at ~55% real-time: aim rotation, power ramp, ball flight and the 1 s hand-off are all in slow motion. title: Unvalidated 'input' message crashes the entire server process
description: server/index.ts:18 casts untrusted JSON to ClientMessage with no shape check and rooms.ts:149 stores message.held verbatim. The try/catch around handleClientMessage does not cover the stored value, which is consumed later in stepRoom -> mergeRoomInput -> snapshotToInput inside the setInterval callback: new Set(123) throws, the exception is uncaught, and Node exits, killing every room. title: Invite-link joiners get stuck in an auto-rejoin loop after any error, and StrictMode double-fires the join opening two sockets
description: The ?room=CODE effect depends on [client, status.kind] and fires whenever status becomes 'idle'. Every error path ends with Cancel/Leave/Back calling client.disconnect() -> setStatus idle -> the effect re-runs -> joinRoom(room) again. The URL is never cleaned with history.replaceState, so a guest with an expired code (host left, server restarted, game ended, since the server destroys the room on any disconnect) gets 'Room not found or full' -> Back -> rejoin, forever, and the same loop rejoins a live room after a deliberate Leave or after OnlineGame remounts Lobby. In React StrictMode (dev) the effect double-fires on mount with no ref guard or cleanup: two WebSockets are created, the second is rejected with 'room full', GameClient.socket points at whichever attached last while the orphaned first socket keeps the host's room full with a phantom guest.

title: Online uses full-state snapshots with no client prediction: every held aim key round-trips through the 60 Hz broadcast, so aiming feels rubbery; keep server-authoritative but move to events + compact snapshots
